Ahmad Fathi, 37; Hamid Firoozi, 34; Amin Shokohi, 25; Sadegh Ahmadzadegan, aka Nitr0jen26, 23; Omid Ghaffarinia, aka PLuS, 25; Sina Keissar, 25; and Nader Saedi, aka Turk Server, 26, launched DDoS attacks against 46 victims, primarily in the U.S financial sector, between late 2011 and mid-2013.\xc2 The attacks disabled victim bank websites, prevented customers from accessing their accounts online and collectively cost the victims tens of millions of dollars in remediation costs as they worked to neutralize and mitigate the attacks on their servers.\xc2 In addition, Firoozi is charged with obtaining unauthorized access into the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems of the Bowman Dam, located in Rye, New York, in August and September of 2013. The indictment was announced today by Attorney General Loretta E. Lynch, Director James B. Comey of the FBI, Assistant Attorney General for National Security John P. Carlin and U.S. Attorney Preet Bharara of the Southern District of New York. \xe2\x80\x9cIn unsealing this indictment, the Department of Justice is sending a powerful message: that we will not allow any individual, group, or nation to sabotage American financial institutions or undermine the integrity of fair competition in the operation of the free market,\xe2\x80\x9d said Attorney General Lynch.\xc2 \xe2\x80\x9cThrough the work of our National Security Division, the FBI, and U.S. Attorney\xe2\x80\x99s Offices around the country, we will continue to pursue national security cyber threats through the use of all available tools, including public criminal charges.\xc2 And as today\xe2\x80\x99s unsealing makes clear, individuals who engage in computer hacking will be exposed for their criminal conduct and sought for apprehension and prosecution in an American court of law.\xe2\x80\x9d \xe2\x80\x9cThe FBI will find those behind cyber intrusions and hold them accountable \xe2\x80\x94 wherever they are, and whoever they are,\xe2\x80\x9d said Director Comey. \xc2 \xe2\x80\x9cBy calling out the individuals and nations who use cyber attacks to threaten American enterprise, as we have done in this indictment, we will change behavior.\xe2\x80\x9d \xe2\x80\x9cLike past nation state-sponsored hackers, these defendants and their backers believed that they could attack our critical infrastructure without consequence, from behind a veil of cyber anonymity,\xe2\x80\x9d said Assistant Attorney General Carlin.\xc2 \xe2\x80\x9cThis indictment once again shows there is no such veil \xe2\x80\x93 we can and will expose malicious cyber hackers engaging in unlawful acts that threaten our public safety and national security.\xe2\x80\x9d \xe2\x80\x9cThe charges announced today respond directly to a cyber-assault on New York, its institutions and its infrastructure,\xe2\x80\x9d said U.S. Attorney Bharara.\xc2 \xe2\x80\x9cThe alleged onslaught of cyber-attacks on 46 of our largest financial institutions, many headquartered in New York City, resulted in hundreds of thousands of customers being unable to access their accounts and tens of millions of dollars being spent by the companies trying to stay online through these attacks.\xc2 The infiltration of the Bowman Avenue dam represents a frightening new frontier in cybercrime.\xc2 These were no ordinary crimes, but calculated attacks by groups with ties to Iran\xe2\x80\x99s Islamic Revolutionary Guard and designed specifically to harm America and its people.\xc2 We now live in a world where devastating attacks on our financial system, our infrastructure and our way of life can be launched from anywhere in the world, with a click of a mouse.\xc2 Confronting these types of cyber-attacks cannot be the job of just law enforcement.\xc2 The charges announced today should serve as a wake-up call for everyone responsible for the security of our financial markets and for guarding our infrastructure.\xc2 Our future security depends on heeding this call.\xe2\x80\x9d According to the indictment unsealed today in federal court in New York City: DDoS Attacks The DDoS campaign began in approximately December 2011, and the attacks occurred only sporadically until September 2012, at which point they escalated in frequency to a near-weekly basis, between Tuesday and Thursdays during normal business hours in the United States.\xc2 On certain days during the campaign, victim computer servers were hit with as much as 140 gigabits of data per second and hundreds of thousands of customers were cut off from online access to their bank accounts.\xc2 Fathi, Firoozi and Shokohi were responsible for ITSEC\xe2\x80\x99s portion of the DDoS campaign against the U.S. financial sector and are charged with one count of conspiracy to commit and aid and abet computer hacking.\xc2 Fathi was the leader of ITSEC and was responsible for supervising and coordinating ITSEC\xe2\x80\x99s portion of the DDoS campaign, along with managing computer intrusion and cyberattack projects being conducted for the government of Iran.\xc2 Firoozi was the network manager at ITSEC and, in that role, procured and managed computer servers that were used to coordinate and direct ITSEC\xe2\x80\x99s portion of the DDoS campaign.\xc2 Shokohi is a computer hacker who helped build the botnet used by ITSEC to carry out its portion of the DDoS campaign and created malware used to direct the botnet to engage in those attacks.\xc2 During the time that he worked in support of the DDoS campaign, Shokohi received credit for his computer intrusion work from the Iranian government towards his completion of his mandatory military service requirement in Iran. Ahmadzadegan, Ghaffarinia, Keissar and Saedi were responsible for managing the botnet used in MERSAD\xe2\x80\x99s portion of the campaign, and are also charged with one count of conspiracy to commit and aid and abet computer hacking.\xc2 Ahmadzadegan was a co-founder of MERSAD and was responsible for managing the botnet used in MERSAD\xe2\x80\x99s portion of the DDoS campaign.\xc2 He was also associated with Iranian hacking groups Sun Army and the Ashiyane Digital Security Team (ADST), and claimed responsibility for hacking servers belonging to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) in February 2012.\xc2 Ahmadzadegan has also provided training to Iranian intelligence personnel.\xc2 Ghaffarinia was a co-founder of MERSAD and created malicious computer code used to compromise computer servers and build MERSAD\xe2\x80\x99s botnet.\xc2 Ghaffarinia was also associated with Sun Army and ADST, and has also claimed responsibility for hacking NASA servers in February 2012, as well as thousands of other servers in the United States, the United Kingdom and Israel.\xc2 Keissar procured computer servers used by MERSAD to access and manipulate MERSAD\xe2\x80\x99s botnet, and also performed preliminary testing of the same botnet prior to its use in MERSAD\xe2\x80\x99s portion of the DDoS campaign.\xc2 Saedi was an employee of MERSAD and a former Sun Army computer hacker who expressly touted himself as an expert in DDoS attacks.\xc2 Saedi wrote computer scripts used to locate vulnerable servers to build the MERSAD botnet used in its portion of the DDoS campaign. For the purpose of carrying out the attacks, each group built and maintained their own botnets, which consisted of thousands of compromised computer systems owned by unwitting third parties that had been infected with the defendants\xe2\x80\x99 malware, and subject to their remote command and control.\xc2 The defendants and/or their unindicted co-conspirators then sent orders to their botnets to direct significant amounts of malicious traffic at computer servers used to operate the websites for victim financial institutions, which overwhelmed victim servers and disabled them from customers seeking to legitimately access the websites or their online bank accounts.\xc2 Although the DDoS campaign caused damage to the financial sector victims and interfered with their customers\xe2\x80\x99 ability to do online banking, the attacks did not affect or result in the theft of customer account data. DDoS Botnet Remediation Since the attacks, the Department of Justice and the FBI have worked together with the private sector to effectively neutralize and remediate the defendants\xe2\x80\x99 botnets.\xc2 Specifically, through approximately 20 FBI Liaison Alert System (FLASH) messages, the FBI regularly provided updated information collected from the investigation regarding the identity of systems that been infected with the defendants\xe2\x80\x99 malware and operating as bots within the malicious botnets.\xc2 In addition, the FBI conducted extensive direct outreach to Internet service providers responsible for hosting systems that have been infected with the defendants\xe2\x80\x99 malware to provide them information and assistance in removing the malware to protect their customers and other potential victims of the defendants\xe2\x80\x99 unlawful cyber activities.\xc2 Through these outreach efforts and the cooperation of the private sector, over 95 percent of the known part of the defendants\xe2\x80\x99 botnets have been successfully remediated. Bowman Dam Intrusion Between Aug. 28, 2013, and Sept. 18, 2013, Firoozi repeatedly obtained unauthorized access to the SCADA systems of the Bowman Dam, and is charged with one substantive count of obtaining and aiding and abetting computer hacking.\xc2 This unauthorized access allowed him to repeatedly obtain information regarding the status and operation of the dam, including information about the water levels, temperature and status of the sluice gate, which is responsible for controlling water levels and flow rates.\xc2 Although that access would normally have permitted Firoozi to remotely operate and manipulate the Bowman Dam\xe2\x80\x99s sluice gate, Firoozi did not have that capability because the sluice gate had been manually disconnected for maintenance at the time of the intrusion. Remediation for the Bowman Dam intrusion cost over $30,000. * * * All seven defendants face a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison for conspiracy to commit and aid and abet computer hacking.\xc2 Firoozi faces an additional five years in prison for obtaining and aiding and abetting unauthorized access to a protected computer at the Bowman Dam. An indictment is merely an accusation and all defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. The case was investigated by the FBI, including the Chicago; Cincinnati; New York; Newark, New Jersey; Phoenix; and San Francisco Field Offices.\xc2 This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Timothy T. Howard of the Southern District of New York, with the substantial assistance of Deputy Chief Sean M. Newell of the National Security Division\xe2\x80\x99s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section.
